title: Off-Broadway’s most provactive and controversial new musical is a bit...
transcript: So I have now seen Slam Frank the hip hop and Frank musical, which, as the merch for the show would like to remind you, is in fact a real musical. Now what I saw was a developmental run, meaning it's very much a work in progress. So this is not meant to be a full review, but rather my initial reactions to the piece, what I think is working well, and what I hope they continue to develop in future runs. Because while I do think there is something here with this show, I also have some qualms with it, which we'll get into. But starting with what I think is working really well. The music in the show goes way harder than it has any right to. Not only is the music catchy as hell, but it is surprisingly intricate both lyrically and Musically, in a way that a lot of satires aren't. I also think for the most part, the satire is really well done. This show really takes aim at so called progressives who weaponize identity politics and the language of progressivism to appear woke and discriminate against people that they don't like while maintaining an imagined position of moral superiority. And I do think that this show could do a better job at differentiating between this specific group of people and people on the left who do genuinely care about diversity, equity and inclusion. Because I do think it's possible to leave the show thinking This is a commentary on the left as a whole, and I don't really think that's what they're going for. One way that it could do this is by leaning harder into the show within a show concept, as the concept of Slam Frank is that the show you are watching is being written and performed by a community theater somewhere in America. As an audience, we're only really seeing the final product. We're not learning anything about all of the decisions that LED to this incredibly misguided outcome. And while we're on the subject of things that I think could be improved upon, I do think the show could benefit from hiring a dramaturg. Which I realize is an incredibly silly thing to say about a musical called Slam Frank, but there are some things that I think this musical gets fundamentally wrong, particularly about the Nazis. It perpetuates this incorrect notion that the Nazis were actually left leaning and supported things like universal healthcare, which they definitely didn't. And they definitely weren't. Yes, their name does stand for National Socialist, but that does not mean that they were actually socialist. And, well, yes, Slam Frank is obviously intentionally historically inaccurate at times. That's where most of its humor is coming from. That particular framing of the Nazis was seemingly presented as true, when it is not. And then you have the final 20 minutes of the show, which I purposely haven't talked about and will not spoil in This video, it kind of becomes a completely different show entirely. And for some people, it's really gonna work, and for others, it's really not gonna work. In my opinion, in its current form, it did not work, and it kind of soured a lot of what had come before it. Which is a shame, because, like I said, a lot of that stuff was genuinely really good. But I do think if, like I said, they work on clarifying intent and showcasing more varied perspectives throughout the piece, it could work. I'm not going to write it off entirely. I do see what they're going for. But it is a fine line, and they are very much riding it.
